hook_text: Fifty-one of a hundred and twenty forms, wasted by three little boxes.
clip_script:
Another class surveys weekly spending at a shopping centre's food court for an economics project. Their question: how much do you spend here in a week. Options: R0 to R20; R20 to R50; R50 to R100. They collect one hundred and twenty forms in a Saturday morning.

Tallying on Monday, they hit trouble three ways. Eleven forms have two ticks, all at the boundaries: people who spend exactly R20 or R50 ticked both boxes they fit. Forty forms have no tick at all, because regular customers spend more than R100 and the top option left them nowhere to go. And a few have a tick plus the note never, because the options had no zero.

Imagine the extremes before you print, and give every boundary exactly one home.
visual_style: Three ticked boxes on a form; forms pile up with double ticks and blank spaces; a redesigned form with six clean intervals slides in over them
call_to_action: Open the full session to design questions that every respondent can answer in exactly one box.
